title: A fixed cohomology degree of derived tensor depends on finite truncation windows
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and use the abelian category of $R$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and its derived category $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Derived tensor is the bifunctor computed by total tensors of K-flat resolutions with flat terms [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Let $K,L\in D(R)$ and $b_K,b_L\in\mathbf Z$ satisfy $H^q(K)=0$ for $q>b_K$ and $H^q(L)=0$ for $q>b_L$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. For every $i\in\mathbf Z$ and integers $a,c$ with $a\leq i-b_L$ and $c\leq i-b_K$, the canonical good-truncation maps [def-kun-truncations] induce an isomorphism of $R$-module sheaves $$H^i(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^i((\tau_{\geq a}K)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}(\tau_{\geq c}L)).$$ The truncated factors have cohomology only in $[a,b_K]$ and $[c,b_L]$, respectively, with the interval interpreted as empty if its lower endpoint exceeds its upper endpoint. No Noetherian, local-constancy, finite-generation, or existence-of-points hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Equip module sheaves with the existing symmetric closed monoidal structure, monoidal preadditivity and functorial flat resolutions at the independent site universes. The existing Grothendieck-abelian theorem applies in coefficient universe max(u,v). These are the hypotheses of the source generic derived monoidal category, not extra hypotheses of the statement.

Use the flat-term K-flat resolving subcategory, its equivalence after localization, and the two natural tensor comparisons of wf_site_derived_tensor_descent. The ordinary complex tensor and the uncurried bifunctor have identity components; their map formulas agree by tensorHom_def. Descend the resulting comparison to the homotopy category by lifting both components of every morphism through its full quotient functor. On the resolving subcategory the source derived tensor counit is invertible: the acyclic-tensor definition gives categorical K-flatness via the homotopy-category acyclic criterion and signed symmetry. Compose the natural comparisons there. Its localization equivalence makes precomposition fully faithful, so this natural isomorphism extends to an isomorphism from wfSiteDerivedTensor to the source derived tensor on all pairs of derived objects.

For the first-factor comparison use the canonical distinguished triangle tau_LE(a-1)K -> K -> tau_GE(a)K. Tensor on the right with L. The source derived tensor functors preserve distinguished triangles; their proof reduces arbitrary derived objects to K-flat homotopy models, as in lem-sc-source-kflat-tensor-left-triangulated, with the right-variable version provided by symmetry. Apply the generic source declaration DerivedCategory.isLE_tensor recorded by lem-weil-pbc-source-derived-tensor-upper-bound to the module-sheaf category. Its first term has upper cohomological bound (a-1)+bL <= i-1. Thus its cohomology in i and i+1 vanishes. The homological-functor long exact sequence makes H^i of the second arrow both monic and epic, hence invertible. The private tensor_truncGE_left theorem is this argument.

The upper bound bK for K is preserved by good lower truncation, including when a>bK. Apply the same triangle argument to L and tensor on the left with tau_GE(a)K. Its discarded first term has bound bK+(c-1) <= i-1. This is the private tensor_truncGE_right theorem. Compose the two induced cohomology isomorphisms using tensorHom_def and functoriality. Naturality of the tensor comparison from Step 2 transfers invertibility to H^i of the specified wfSiteDerivedTensor image of the two canonical truncation maps; an arbitrary objectwise tensor isomorphism would not suffice.

The standard t-structure gives tau_GE(a)K lower bound a and preserves its upper bound bK, and gives tau_GE(c)L lower bound c and preserves upper bound bL. Translate these bounds to zero cohomology outside the two stated intervals. If a>bK or c>bL, every integer lies outside the relevant interval, so this proof also covers empty windows.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q111-248a179da (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all five steps in full, together with the statement of every cited node; there are no new nodes and no files were changed. Source: Stacks 094H (sites-cohomology.tex 14356-14376). Its uniform cutoff tau_{>=i-1} is false: on the one-point site over a field k, K=k[2], L=k[-2], i=0 gives H^0 of the tensor equal to k, but tau_{>=-1}K=0. The item's corrected cutoffs a<=i-b_L and c<=i-b_K are correct and not weakened, and the only citer (lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-tensor) uses exactly these. Step 1: the good-truncation windows follow from def-kun-truncations. Step 2: lem-pc-kflat-bounded-flat-replacement keeps the term bound N, lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site gives K-flatness, and the descent node gives the Tot model; the hypotheses (same small site, same commutative R) hold. Step 3: the degree count is correct; the Tot terms vanish for n>a-1+b_L and for n>b_K+c-1, both at most i-1, so H^i and H^{i+1} of both tails are zero. Steps 4-5: the truncation triangle (Mathlib leaf, matches derived.tex 08J5), the 'exact in each variable' sentence of lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact (its proof uses the descent node, so it is the same bifunctor) and the long exact sequence leaf give two isomorphisms, and bifunctoriality makes their composite H^i(q_K tensor q_L). proof_deps equals the union of uses, and the graph stays acyclic (the item is not in the 484-node dependency closure of its citations). Route: the descent and mate-exact nodes are in the same unit and both lem-sf nodes are Mathlib leaves. The two declared tool uses (lem-pc-kflat-bounded-flat-replacement, lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site) are accepted as generic black boxes. Duplicate search: lem-kun-derived-tensor-t-est, lem-kun-integral-derived-tensor-bounded-torsion, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-cohomological-bounds, prop-weil-pbc-levelwise-truncations and lem-sf-tensor-ctf do not state this result. Small cases checked: the shifted counterexample, endpoint equality, empty windows, acyclic factors, and Z/2 tensor Z/2 over Z. No SGA source is cited. lean.statement: theorem isIso_derivedTensor_truncationWindow {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{max u v}) [HasDerivedCategory.{w, max u v, (max u v) + 1} (SheafOfModules.{max u v, v, u, max u v} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u v} RingCat.{max u v})).obj R))] (K L : DerivedCategory.{w, max u v, (max u v) + 1} (SheafOfModules.{max u v, v, u, max u v} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u v} RingCat.{max u v})).obj R))) (bK bL : ℤ) (hK : ∀ q : ℤ, bK < q → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj K)) (hL : ∀ q : ℤ, bL < q → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj L)) (i a c : ℤ) (ha : a ≤ i - bL) (hc : c ≤ i - bK) : IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).map ((wfSiteDerivedTensor J R).map (CategoryTheory.Prod.mkHom ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ a).app K) ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ c).app L)))) ∧ (∀ q : ℤ, q < a ∨ bK < q → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGE a).obj K))) ∧ (∀ q : ℤ, q < c ∨ bL < q → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGE c).obj L)))
